tasks.title: Fold PropDef.Yaw into MapData.Hash's field-by-field prop loop
tasks.why: MapData.Hash (MapData.cs:309-313) hashes Props field by field to dodge struct padding, but the list it folds in is Pos, Hp, Scale, Cell, Kind only -- Yaw is left out. Yaw is authoritative sim state: BattlefieldGenerator.cs:321,327,329 sets it from the seeded RNG for every tree and wreck, and Deformation.cs:108-109 sets a wreck's Yaw from the dying vehicle's heading (d.Yaw) at AddProp. Nothing in Sim/** reads PropDef.Yaw for a rule (confirmed by grep: every other '.Yaw' hit is a vehicle or unit field), so today it is cosmetic, but it is the one piece of prop state the hash chain cannot see: a future rule that reads it, or a presentation bug that assumes replay-identical worlds also agree on it, has no test or determinism check that would ever catch a divergence.
tasks.done_when: A new EditMode test builds two MapData instances, AddProp's the same PropDef into each except for Yaw, and asserts Hash(0) differs; red on this commit (Yaw omitted, hashes equal) and green once MapData.cs:312 adds `h = SimHash.Value(p.Yaw, h);` with a SimHash/FormatVersion bump logged in docs/02-contracts.md. Determinism, replay and hash tests rerun green after.

tasks.title: MapData.RebuildCover rescans every prop on every single stage change
tasks.why: MapData.SetPropKind (MapData.cs:202-213), called once per prop that finishes breaking (PropHarm.Harm -> SetPropKind via Deformation.Shake), calls RebuildCover (MapData.cs:215-220) unconditionally: it zeroes the whole CellCover array and restamps every prop in map.Props from scratch, every time, even though only one prop's cover percent changed. A barrage in a wood (PropIndexTests' 400-tree forest is the measured case) can finish several trees in the same tick -- Shake (Deformation.cs:151-184) calls PropHarm.Harm per candidate, each Changed outcome re-walking all 400+ props -- so one tick's cost is O(props-changed x total-props) where it only needs to touch the handful of cells those props actually stamp.
tasks.done_when: A bench (CaptureRig.Bench or a new EditMode timing test) on PropIndexTests' 400-tree forest barrage shows RebuildCover's share of the tick down after the fix; BattlefieldTests.Blasts_WearATreeDownToAStump_AndItsCoverAndBlockedCellGoWithIt and the determinism/replay/hash tests stay green and unmoved.

tasks.title: WireBelt.Place and MudField.Place duplicate the same rect-fill loop
tasks.why: WireBelt.cs:12-22 and MudField.cs:13-23 are identical except for the one NavLayer bit they add (Wire vs Mud) and the layer-skip set they both test (Trench | Link | Bunker | Blocked). A fix to the skip set, the NavCellOf rounding, or the SetLayer call in one (e.g. the fault class the owner's wire-gap frame decision and the 2026-09-28 mud-cost note both touch) has to be remembered and made twice; nothing enforces that the second copy follows.
tasks.done_when: WireBelt.Place and MudField.Place call one shared MapData helper (e.g. MapData.FillRect(min, max, NavLayer, skipMask)) differing only in the layer bit; BattlefieldTests and DynamicGroundTests pass unchanged, and determinism/replay/hash tests stay green.
